root_causes.description: The recommendation service pod consumes an anomalous amount of CPU during the incident window (mean 2.343 cores, p95/p99 ~3.60, peak 3.608), ~33x higher than frontend (0.070) and ~94x higher than product-catalog (0.025). Error rate, memory usage and pod restarts remain at baseline, which is the exact signature of an injected CPU-stress fault rather than a crash, latency, memory or dependency failure.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate=0.000 (flat at zero across the window)

evidence.expected_baseline: stable ~106 MB (no memory growth / no pressure)

root_causes.description: Frontend is a direct upstream caller of recommendation (frontend -> recommendation in the topology), so if the recommendation CPU saturation degrades recommendation response quality, frontend latency could rise as a secondary effect. No frontend error or resource anomaly was observed in this session, so this remains a weak secondary hypothesis.

Product-catalog is the downstream dependency of recommendation (recommendation -> product-catalog). If recommendation's CPU stress caused timeouts or request failures toward product-catalog, downstream symptoms could appear there, but product-catalog CPU is at baseline (0.025) and no error/restart signal was seen, so this is unlikely.

remediation_steps: Confirm the CPU saturation source on the recommendation pod: kubectl top pods -n otel-demo and inspect for a stress-ng / busy-loop sidecar or injected fault marked seed42.
If the fault is injected, stop/disable the CPU-stress experiment targeting the recommendation service (remove the chaos/fault injection).
Verify recommendation CPU usage returns to baseline (~0.03-0.07 cores) after the fault is removed and confirm frontend request latency/quality normalizes (frontend depends on recommendation).
Add a CPU-usage alert on the recommendation deployment to catch similar sustained, error-free CPU saturation in the future.
